units.function: Express regression test proving the static folder-item move route is selected before the parameterized folder reorder route.
units.dependencyDirection: A board-authenticated HTTP request enters the folder router with mocked services; route matching must dispatch item movement to folderService.moveItem rather than moveFolder.
units.keyDataModels: Company ID, folder kind, item UUID, optional folder UUID and board actor context.
units.lifecycle: POST /companies/:companyId/folders/items/move is validated, dispatched once to moveItem and must never reach the later /folders/:folderId/move handler.
units.testAssessment: The regression precisely catches an Express route-order collision and verifies the service call shape. It does not assert Company-access denial, invalid payloads, activity evidence, service failures, missing targets, response error codes, other actor types or transaction behavior.
units.designRationale: Keep a literal path segment from being captured as the :folderId parameter of a broader route declared nearby.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deterministic API routing for organization, evidence and FDE asset hierarchies, with tests that prevent broad identifiers from shadowing command endpoints.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the route-specificity regression pattern, while preferring resource-oriented command paths or a generated router that rejects ambiguous templates and adding authorization, validation and audit assertions.
units.responsibilityConflict: The mocked test proves dispatch only; it cannot prove that the caller had authority, that the moved item belongs to the Company, or that the resulting activity record forms responsibility evidence.

units.function: Company-scoped HTTP CRUD and move routes for routine/skill folders, including creation of a signed-in board user's personal skill folder and activity logging after mutations.
units.dependencyDirection: Express and shared Zod validators feed assertCompanyAccess and folderService; successful mutations then call the activity logger and serialize service results.
units.keyDataModels: Folder ID/company/kind/parent/name/slug/path/depth/color/position/system key, routine or company-skill item reference, board/agent actor metadata and activity details.
units.lifecycle: List parses a required kind; create/update/move/delete validate Company access, mutate through the service, log an activity after success and return JSON; ensure-my additionally requires a signed-in board user.
units.testAssessment: The route file centralizes Company access checks and validates mutation bodies, but its dedicated test covers only the route-order regression. There is no route-level evidence here for access denial, cross-Company IDs, personal-folder ownership, logger failure after mutation, idempotency, concurrency, stable structured errors or rollback consistency.
units.designRationale: Expose a thin authenticated HTTP layer over a folder service and retain actor-attributed operational history without putting hierarchy logic in Express handlers.
units.companyOsProblem: FDE templates, evidence collections and office configuration may need tenant-scoped hierarchies and human-owned private areas without allowing transport code to become the policy owner.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the thin route/service split, Company guard and post-mutation actor context. Company OS must use stable error codes, policy-scoped Principal authorization, idempotent commands and an atomic outbox/event transaction so state cannot commit while its responsibility evidence fails.
units.responsibilityConflict: Mutation and activity logging are separate awaits with no visible atomicity; an activity logger failure can follow a committed mutation. Generic actor metadata also lacks the Work, responsibility contract, approval, data scope and evidence bindings required for consequential changes.

units.function: Pure unit tests normalizing absent, scalar, CSV, repeated and mixed Express query values into a trimmed Issue-status list.
units.dependencyDirection: Untrusted query-parser output enters parseStatusFilter; normalized strings are later consumed by Company-scoped Drizzle equality or IN predicates in Issue list/count services.
units.keyDataModels: Undefined, string or readonly string-array query values and an ordered string-array status filter.
units.lifecycle: The helper copies arrays, splits each string on commas, trims values, removes empties and silently drops non-string entries before database predicates are constructed.
units.testAssessment: Coverage is strong for legitimate Express encodings, whitespace, empty entries, immutability and hostile non-string array members. Missing are status-enum validation, duplicate removal, maximum item/value length, encoded delimiter behavior, unsupported object shapes, stable validation errors and proof that every service caller applies identical authorization and pagination.
units.designRationale: Repair a production 500 caused by assuming repeated query keys were always one string while preserving existing CSV clients.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Web, mobile and FDE clients need one bounded, schema-defined multi-value filter contract that never crashes on transport-specific query shapes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the normalization cases into a shared API-boundary primitive, then validate against canonical status codes, deduplicate, cap cardinality and length, and return a stable INVALID_ARGUMENT code with structured parameters rather than silently accepting unknown states.
units.responsibilityConflict: Permissive arbitrary status strings can hide operator mistakes by returning an empty view, which is unsafe for approval and exception queues; filters must never be mistaken for authorization or evidence-access policy.
